sourcing_notes: Reached everything needed. (1) nvidianews.nvidia.com/releases.xml returned HTTP 200 with 20 <item> elements, newest 2026-09-16 — but its oldest item was 2026-09-01, so the target release was not in it. Walking ?page=3 (HTTP 200, 20 items) surfaced the real link and the official pubDate Mon, 31 Aug 2026 12:30:00 GMT / modDate 12:35:28 GMT. (2) The NVIDIA release page itself, https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-and-mediatek-deepen-long-standing-partnership-to-build-ai-edge-to-cloud-computing-platforms, returned HTTP 200, 82,927 bytes, correct <title>; I read the full body. WARNING for later agents: a shortened guess of that slug ('...-deepen-long-standing-partnership') also returns HTTP 200, 68,941 bytes, but the body is the generic 'News Archive | NVIDIA Newsroom' page. Status code alone would have hidden the soft-404. (3) MediaTek: corp.mediatek.com/news-events/press-releases 301s to www.mediatek.com/press-room (HTTP 200); www.mediatek.com/news-events/press-releases is 404. The press-room RSS at www.mediatek.com/press-room/rss.xml returned HTTP 200 with 10 items, newest 2026-09-15 — a live feed. Both the English and the zh-TW versions of the joint release returned HTTP 200 and were read in full. (4) Taiwan MOPS: emops.twse.com.tw and mops.twse.com.tw both return a security-block page to curl from this container ('FOR SECURITY REASONS, THIS PAGE CAN NOT BE ACCESSED', error code shown). WebFetch reached them. I used only URLs that MediaTek's own investor-relations page links to, plus the two detail links that the listing page's own gotoURL() markup contains — nothing was guessed. Because the MOPS figures came through WebFetch's text extraction rather than raw HTML I could inspect, I ran three independent passes over the 2026-08-31 filing asking for verbatim field text and they agreed, and the numbers are internally consistent: 17,500 certificates x US$200,000 denomination = US$3,500,000 thousand, and NT$4,513.75 / 1.15 = NT$3,925.00 exactly, matching the quoted closing price. I am treating those figures as reliable but the writer should attribute them to MediaTek's MOPS filing, not to the press release. (5) SEC: efts.sec.gov full-text search API returned HTTP 200. 'MediaTek' within NVIDIA's CIK 0001045810 gives 12 hits, none after 2024-02-21; a 2026-08-01 to 2026-09-16 all-filer search surfaced no NVIDIA filing. So there is no US filing to cite. (6) sec.gov itself, openai.com/index/*, pr.tsmc.com and news.samsung.com were not needed and were not retried.

sources.title: MediaTek Collaborates with NVIDIA on RTX Spark to Power the Next Wave of Windows PC Experiences

event_date_basis: 2026-08-31 is the announcement date and is what the slug and news_date must carry. Both companies' datelines read August 31, 2026 ('SANTA CLARA, Calif.—AUGUST 31, 2026'; 「2026 年 8 月 31 日美國聖塔克拉訊」). NVIDIA's official feed gives pubDate Mon, 31 Aug 2026 12:30:00 GMT and modDate Mon, 31 Aug 2026 12:35:28 GMT — 12:30 GMT is 20:30 on 31 August Taipei time. MediaTek's own CMS timestamps disagree between locales: the zh-TW page carries 2026-08-31 12:30:00 while the English page carries 2026-08-30 21:40:00 (displayed as 'Aug 31, 2026 - 05:40 AM'), and MediaTek's RSS repeats the 30 Aug 21:40 GMT value for the English page. The datelines on both pages still say August 31, so the discrepancy is a publishing-system artefact, not a different event date. Publication and effective dates differ from the event date and must not be conflated: MediaTek's board resolved to issue the bonds on 2026-07-31; pricing completed and was filed on MOPS on 2026-08-31 at 20:25:52 Taipei (about five minutes before the press release); the bonds' TENTATIVE issue date is 2026/09/08 and tentative maturity 2031/09/08; conversion cannot start until three months after issuance. As of the 2026-09-16 check there is no MOPS announcement confirming the issuance actually completed.

verified_facts.fact: The announcement is dated August 31, 2026 and datelined Santa Clara, California. NVIDIA's newsroom page prints the date 'August 31, 2026'; MediaTek's English page opens 'SANTA CLARA, Calif.—AUGUST 31, 2026'.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: August 31, 2026

verified_facts.fact: The official English title is 'NVIDIA and MediaTek Deepen Long-Standing Partnership to Build AI Edge to Cloud Computing Platforms'.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: NVIDIA and MediaTek Deepen Long-Standing Partnership to Build AI Edge to Cloud Computing Platforms

verified_facts.fact: The release carries two official subheadings.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Companies Expand Collaboration Across Multigenerational Cloud AI Factories, Local AI Computing and Automotive | MediaTek to Adopt New NVIDIA NVLink Fusion Platform, Helping Customers Take Custom XPUs to NVIDIA NVLink-Connected, Rack-Scale AI Factories

verified_facts.fact: The core announcement is a deepening of an existing collaboration, not a new partnership and not a product launch.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: NVIDIA and MediaTek today announced a deepening of their longstanding collaboration to build the next generations of AI computing platforms — spanning AI infrastructure, local AI computing and automotive.

verified_facts.fact: MediaTek will adopt the NVIDIA NVLink Fusion platform to give hyperscalers, cloud service providers and frontier model developers a prevalidated path to develop custom XPUs and bring them into NVIDIA NVLink-connected, rack-scale AI factories.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: As part of the expanded collaboration, MediaTek will adopt the NVIDIA NVLink Fusion™ platform to provide hyperscalers, cloud service providers and frontier model developers with a prevalidated path to develop custom XPUs and bring them into NVIDIA NVLink™-connected, rack-scale AI factories.

verified_facts.fact: NVIDIA says it combines its accelerated computing, AI, graphics and software platforms with MediaTek's custom silicon, high-performance computing, power-efficient SoC design, advanced packaging, interconnects and connectivity.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: The companies combine NVIDIA’s accelerated computing, AI, graphics and software platforms with MediaTek’s leadership in custom silicon, high-performance computing, power-efficient system-on-chip (SoC) design, advanced packaging, interconnects and connectivity.

verified_facts.fact: NVIDIA has invested US$3.5 billion in convertible bonds issued by MediaTek. This is the only financial figure in the press release, and the release gives no other terms.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: NVIDIA has also invested $3.5 billion in convertible bonds issued by MediaTek.

verified_facts.fact: MediaTek's own Traditional Chinese release is more specific than the English one about the instrument: it calls it 海外可轉換公司債（ECB） (overseas convertible bond) and states the amount as 美金 35 億元.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: NVIDIA 同時投資美金 35 億元於聯發科技發行的海外可轉換公司債（ECB）。

verified_facts.fact: The official Traditional Chinese title MediaTek uses is 「NVIDIA 與聯發科技深化長期合作夥伴關係共同打造從邊緣到雲端的 AI 運算平台」.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: NVIDIA 與聯發科技深化長期合作夥伴關係共同打造從邊緣到雲端的 AI 運算平台

verified_facts.fact: The collaboration is described as covering three major areas: AI infrastructure, local AI computing, and automotive.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: NVIDIA and MediaTek are collaborating in three major areas:

verified_facts.fact: AI infrastructure area: MediaTek will work with NVIDIA's NVLink Fusion ecosystem so customers can develop custom AI infrastructure that integrates with NVIDIA rack-scale systems and AI factories.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: AI infrastructure: MediaTek will work with NVIDIA’s NVLink Fusion ecosystem to enable customers to develop custom AI infrastructure designed to integrate with NVIDIA rack-scale systems and AI factories.

verified_facts.fact: Local AI computing area: the companies will continue to collaborate on multiple generations of NVIDIA RTX Spark and DGX Spark PC chips for consumer PCs, AI developer supercomputers and enterprise-class workstations, integrating NVIDIA GPUs with MediaTek SoCs. No generation is named, dated or specified.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Local AI computing: The companies will continue to collaborate on multiple generations of NVIDIA RTX Spark™ and DGX Spark™ PC chips, powering consumer PCs, AI developer supercomputers and enterprise-class workstations, that integrate NVIDIA GPUs with MediaTek SoCs.

verified_facts.fact: MediaTek's zh-TW release labels this same bullet 邊緣 AI 運算 (edge AI computing), where the English release says 'Local AI computing'. They are the same bullet, not two separate programmes.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: 邊緣 AI 運算：雙方將持續合作開發未來數代 RTX Spark™ 與 DGX Spark™ 電腦晶片

verified_facts.fact: Automotive area: MediaTek and NVIDIA will continue developing platforms for AI-powered, software-defined vehicles in the era of physical AI. No vehicle, brand, model or date is given.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Automotive: MediaTek and NVIDIA will continue developing platforms for AI-powered, software-defined vehicles in the era of physical AI.

verified_facts.fact: NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang is quoted saying AI is transforming every computing platform and that the two companies are building platforms that bring NVIDIA accelerated computing to new markets. This is a company statement, not an independently verified claim.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: “AI is transforming every computing platform — from the world’s largest AI factories to the PC and the car,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “MediaTek is one of the world’s great semiconductor companies, with exceptional expertise in system-on-chip design, connectivity, leading performance and power efficiency. Together, we’re building platforms that bring NVIDIA accelerated computing to new markets and give customers the freedom to create differentiated AI systems at enormous scale.”

verified_facts.fact: Rick Tsai is identified as vice chairman and CEO of MediaTek (zh-TW: 聯發科技副董事長暨執行長蔡力行); he is quoted saying NVIDIA's investment strengthens a collaboration spanning cloud AI infrastructure, local AI computing and automotive. Company statement, not fact.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: “MediaTek and NVIDIA share a vision for making advanced AI computing pervasive across the technology landscape,” said Rick Tsai, vice chairman and CEO of MediaTek. “NVIDIA’s investment strengthens a collaboration that spans cloud AI infrastructure, local AI computing and automotive in the era of physical AI.

verified_facts.fact: MediaTek will offer the NVLink Fusion platform as a design foundation for customers developing custom AI accelerators, so their platforms can evolve alongside future NVIDIA architectures.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: MediaTek will offer the NVLink Fusion platform as a design foundation for customers developing custom AI accelerators, enabling their platforms to evolve alongside future NVIDIA architectures.

verified_facts.fact: NVIDIA describes the NVLink Fusion platform as a prebuilt, prequalified and system-prevalidated foundation for multi-die XPU development. This is a vendor description of its own product.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: The NVLink Fusion platform provides a prebuilt, prequalified and system-prevalidated foundation for multi-die XPU development — accelerating the path from silicon and advanced packaging to rack-scale systems.

verified_facts.fact: The NVLink Fusion platform is said to bring together three named technologies: the NVIDIA NVLink Fusion chiplet, NVIDIA NVLink-C2C, and NVIDIA NVHBM.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: The NVLink Fusion platform brings together the critical technologies surrounding a custom XPU, including:

verified_facts.fact: The NVLink Fusion chiplet connects XPUs to the NVIDIA NVLink scale-up fabric using NVIDIA photonics or electrical interconnects.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: NVIDIA NVLink Fusion chiplet, connecting XPUs to the NVIDIA NVLink scale-up fabric using NVIDIA photonics or electrical interconnects.

verified_facts.fact: NVLink-C2C is described as providing high-bandwidth, energy-efficient connectivity between XPUs, NVIDIA Rosa CPUs and other compatible processors. 'NVIDIA Rosa CPUs' is the wording used in both companies' releases; neither release explains what a Rosa CPU is or when it ships.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: NVIDIA NVLink-C2C, providing high-bandwidth, energy-efficient connectivity between XPUs, NVIDIA Rosa CPUs and other compatible processors.

verified_facts.fact: NVHBM is described as integrating customized memory capabilities to increase bandwidth and energy efficiency while dedicating more silicon area to compute. Vendor description; no figures given.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: NVIDIA NVHBM, integrating customized memory capabilities to increase bandwidth and energy efficiency while dedicating more silicon area to compute.

verified_facts.fact: The division of labour stated: customers focus on differentiated compute while NVIDIA and MediaTek supply the NVLink connectivity, memory architecture, packaging, manufacturing and rack-scale technologies needed for production deployment.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Rather than engineering and qualifying every element surrounding a custom XPU from the ground up, customers can focus resources on the differentiated compute that defines their platforms while relying on NVIDIA and MediaTek for the NVLink connectivity, memory architecture, packaging, manufacturing and rack-scale technologies required for production deployment.

verified_facts.fact: Customers can bring their XPU designs to MediaTek and tailor connectivity, memory, packaging, performance and power characteristics to their workloads and infrastructure requirements.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Customers can bring their XPU designs to MediaTek and tailor connectivity, memory, packaging, performance and power characteristics to their workloads and infrastructure requirements.

verified_facts.fact: MediaTek is described as part of the broader NVIDIA NVLink Fusion ecosystem; the NVIDIA MGX rack-scale architecture is named as part of the stack partners can use. NVIDIA claims this reduces development complexity, increases performance and accelerates time to market for semi-custom AI factories.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: With NVLink Fusion, partners can leverage NVIDIA’s proven scale-up and scale-out technology stack and ecosystem, as well as the NVIDIA MGX™ rack-scale architecture, to reduce development complexity, increase performance and accelerate time to market for semi-custom AI factories.

verified_facts.fact: Existing work cited: MediaTek collaborated with NVIDIA on the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip that powers NVIDIA DGX Spark, which combines an NVIDIA Blackwell GPU and Grace CPU connected by NVLink-C2C.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: MediaTek collaborated with NVIDIA on the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip that powers NVIDIA DGX Spark, which combines an NVIDIA Blackwell GPU and Grace CPU connected by NVLink-C2C to bring powerful AI capabilities to edge systems.

verified_facts.fact: The companies say they have extended that collaboration with NVIDIA RTX Spark to power the next generation of consumer PCs. The 31 Aug release announces no RTX Spark product, price or date.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: The companies have extended their collaboration with NVIDIA RTX Spark to power the next generation of consumer PCs redefined for the AI era.

verified_facts.fact: Automotive detail: MediaTek Dimensity Auto platforms integrate NVIDIA technologies to deliver advanced AI and NVIDIA RTX graphics for intelligent vehicle cockpits and can work alongside NVIDIA DRIVE AGX. The release says the companies will continue across future generations.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: MediaTek Dimensity Auto platforms integrate NVIDIA technologies to deliver advanced AI and NVIDIA RTX™ graphics for intelligent vehicle cockpits and can work alongside NVIDIA DRIVE AGX™.

verified_facts.fact: Boilerplate identifiers: MediaTek is listed as TWSE: 2454 and described as a fabless semiconductor design company; NVIDIA is NASDAQ: NVDA.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: MediaTek (TWSE: 2454) is a global leader in fabless semiconductor design, powering AI from the edge to the cloud.

verified_facts.fact: MediaTek attaches a forward-looking statement saying the release relates solely to the business collaboration, does not constitute forecast information under applicable Taiwan laws and regulations, and that MediaTek makes no representation, warranty or assurance regarding achievement of any anticipated objectives, milestones, performance or results. It also tells investors to exercise independent judgment.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: It does not constitute, and should not be construed as, any business, operational, financial, revenue, earnings, or other forecast information under applicable Taiwan laws and regulations.

verified_facts.fact: That MediaTek forward-looking statement appears on the English pages (NVIDIA newsroom and MediaTek English) but is NOT reproduced on MediaTek's zh-TW page, which ends at the About sections.
NVIDIA's official news feed timestamps the release at Mon, 31 Aug 2026 12:30:00 GMT with a modDate of Mon, 31 Aug 2026 12:35:28 GMT (12:30 GMT = 20:30 Taipei time).

verified_facts.verbatim_quote: said Vince Hu, Corporate Senior Vice President at MediaTek and head of the company’s compute platforms, data center solutions and IoT businesses

not_said: Neither company's press release states the TOTAL size of the convertible bond issue, the coupon, the maturity, the conversion price, the conversion period, the dilution, the listing venue or the issue date. The only figure in the release is NVIDIA's US$3.5 billion. All of the other terms come from MediaTek's MOPS statutory filing of 2026-08-31, and the article must attribute them there, not to the press release.

The press release does not say NVIDIA has become a MediaTek shareholder. Convertible bonds are not shares until converted; per the MOPS filing conversion cannot begin until three months after issuance.

Neither the press release nor the MOPS filing states what percentage of MediaTek NVIDIA itself would hold if it converted only its own US$3.5 billion. The ~1.67% figure is the maximum dilution of the whole US$3.9 billion issue.
The MOPS filing names no subscriber other than NVIDIA and does not say how the remaining roughly US$0.4 billion of the issue was placed.

No product is launched, named as a new model, or dated on 2026-08-31. 'Multiple generations of NVIDIA RTX Spark and DGX Spark PC chips' is the entire product statement — no generation names, no specifications, no process node, no clock speeds, no memory figures, no launch window.
No prices are given for anything — no chip pricing, no PC pricing, no licensing or royalty terms for the NVLink Fusion work.

No volumes, unit forecasts, wafer commitments, capacity reservations or revenue figures. MediaTek's own forward-looking statement expressly says the release is not any business, operational, financial, revenue or earnings forecast under Taiwan law.
No customers are named for the custom XPU / NVLink Fusion business. No design wins, no hyperscaler, no cloud service provider, no frontier model developer is identified.
No automaker, vehicle brand, model or production date is named for the Dimensity Auto / DRIVE AGX work, and no start-of-production date is given.

No foundry, packaging house or memory supplier is named in the 31 August release. TSMC appears only in MediaTek's separate 2026-06-01 RTX Spark release, and only as MediaTek's manufacturing partner for that SoC.

No regions, no country availability, and nothing at all about Taiwan availability, Taiwan pricing or a Taiwan launch. The release is a corporate and technology announcement, not a consumer availability announcement.
No regulatory approval, antitrust review, export-control condition or closing condition is mentioned for the investment, and no closing date is given for it.
No governance terms: no board seat, no observer right, no exclusivity, no standstill, no lock-up, no minimum purchase commitment is mentioned.
No benchmark, throughput, bandwidth, power or efficiency number appears anywhere in the 31 August release. Every capability statement is qualitative.
The release does not say when NVLink Fusion chiplet, NVLink-C2C, NVHBM or the 'NVIDIA Rosa CPUs' it names become available, nor what a Rosa CPU is.
The release does not restate or update the 'Fall 2026' first-wave RTX Spark laptop timing from MediaTek's 2026-06-01 release, and it does not say whether that timing still holds.

As of the check date 2026-09-16 there is no MediaTek MOPS announcement confirming that the bond issuance actually completed on the tentative 2026/09/08 issue date, so the article must call that date tentative.

Neither company says the collaboration is new or exclusive; both call it a deepening of a long-standing collaboration, and MediaTek's own June 2026 release already listed NVLink Fusion, GB10 and the C-X1 automotive platform as existing work.

Do not write that NVIDIA bought a stake in MediaTek, became a shareholder, or 'took equity'. It subscribed to convertible bonds. Conversion cannot begin until three months after the issue date, and the issue date itself is still tentative.
Do not write '稀釋 1.67%' as NVIDIA's stake. 1.67% is the maximum dilution of the whole US$3.9 billion issue assuming full conversion within the year, per MediaTek's filing.

editorial_brief: WHO IT IS FOR: Taiwanese readers who follow technology but are not chip engineers, and who care because MediaTek (聯發科技, TWSE 2454) is a Taiwanese company whose disclosures land on MOPS in Chinese. The angle is not 'NVIDIA is huge'. It is: on one evening, 31 August 2026, two chip companies published a partnership announcement in English, and within about five minutes of each other a Taiwanese listed company filed the money side of the same event with its own regulator — and the two documents say different amounts of things. Reading both is what tells you what actually happened. STRUCTURE THAT FITS THE FACTS (five level-2 sections per BRIEF): (1) What was announced on 31 August 2026 — a deepening of an existing collaboration across three named areas, plus the one financial line the press release carries. (2) The three areas explained plainly: custom XPUs via NVLink Fusion for rack-scale AI factories; PC chips (RTX Spark, DGX Spark); automotive (Dimensity Auto alongside DRIVE AGX). End this section with the required table. (3) The money: what MediaTek told MOPS that the press release never said — first overseas convertible bond issue, US$3.9bn total of which NVIDIA took US$3.5bn, 0% coupon, NT$4,513.75 conversion price at 115% of the NT$3,925 close, tentative 2026/09/08 issue and 2031/09/08 maturity, SGX, approximately 1.67% maximum dilution. End this section with the diagram. (4) What this is NOT — no product, no price, no date, no customer, no Taiwan availability; and MediaTek's own forward-looking statement saying the release is not a forecast under Taiwan law. (5) What would actually tell you whether it is working — the tentative issue date passing, a named XPU customer, a named next-generation Spark chip, a named car. Frame these as things to watch that are currently unstated, not as predictions. TABLE SUGGESTION (3 columns, 4 rows, cells short, caption carries the check date 2026-09-16): columns 「合作領域」/「官方點名的技術」/「官方未說明」; rows AI 基礎建設 / 邊緣與本地 AI 運算 / 車用 / 投資. DIAGRAM SUGGESTION (2x2, four nodes, every number in it must also be in the body): 「三大領域」「一筆投資」「申報才有的條件」「官方未說」. Title under 20 characters, e.g. 「一則公告的兩個版本」. Hero label under 12 characters, e.g. 「合作公告，不是新產品」. ORIGINAL SCENARIO (must be labelled as an editorially constructed example): a reader who sees a headline about 'NVIDIA investing in MediaTek' and wants to know whether that means a new laptop chip is coming, or shares changing hands — the answer is neither, and the article shows how to tell by comparing the press release with the MOPS filing. DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE: share-price movement, valuation, whether the bonds are a good deal, any comparison of MediaTek against Qualcomm or others, any buying advice about RTX Spark PCs, and any speculation about which hyperscaler the custom-XPU business is for. Also out of scope: the NVIDIA-Hugging Face acquisition, which is a separate pack in this batch. TONE: plain and specific. Every capability sentence attributed to the company that said it. State the check date 2026-09-16 in the second paragraph and say the site did no hands-on testing.
